goal: Let Claude Code invoke the existing resume-tailoring skill in this project without changing the approved architecture.
authorization: User approved the project-level option only (no global ~/.claude/skills install, install_skill.py unchanged).
changes: Added CLAUDE.md that imports AGENTS.md so Claude Code loads the same project rules.
Created directory junction .claude/skills/resume-tailoring -> skills/resume-tailoring (single skill source shared with Codex).
Made SKILL.md agent-neutral and added trigger guidance to its description.
Updated AGENTS.md first line and README usage/setup for Claude Code.
rationale: Claude Code and Codex share the SKILL.md format, so a junction avoids a drifting copy; an @import keeps AGENTS.md as the only rule source. Helpers, templates, rubric and output layout are untouched.
expected_behavior: In a Claude Code session opened in this workspace, /resume-tailoring is available (and may auto-trigger on a pasted job posting); AGENTS.md rules are in context. Codex behavior is unchanged apart from the wording/description update.
assumptions: Claude Code follows NTFS directory junctions when discovering project skills (confirmed by the validation below).

validation.unit_tests: python -m unittest discover -s tests: Ran 3 tests, OK
validation.headless_rules_loaded: claude -p quoted the AGENTS.md sentence about template/ being immutable

known_issues: Junction is a local filesystem object; a fresh clone or copy needs it recreated (README gives CMD commands). If the project becomes a git repo, the junction should not be committed as a directory copy.
Recursive deletion of .claude/skills/resume-tailoring could delete the real skill files; use rmdir on the junction only.
Installed Codex copy in ~/.codex/skills is not synced automatically; run install_skill.py --update if Codex should get the new SKILL.md wording.
next_steps: Run one real tailoring task in Claude Code to confirm end-to-end behavior (prepare, build, PNG inspection, scoring).
